## Yesterday: a document. Today: a body of work. {.section-divider}

::: {.notes}
⏱️ 2 min. Same machinery, different organisation. Nothing new to learn about
chunks — this session is about structure.
:::

## Pick your output

| Output | Format | For |
|---|---|---|
| Manuscript | `docx` + `pdf` | Journals |
| Slides | `revealjs` | Conferences |
| Website | `type: website` | Course sites |
| Thesis | `type: book` | Chapters |
| Dashboard | `dashboard` | Surveillance |

Same Markdown. Same chunks.

## Split it up

```
thesis/
├── index.qmd
├── 01-introduction.qmd
├── 02-methods.qmd
├── 03-results.qmd
└── references.bib
```

Or inline: `{{{< include _methods.qmd >}}}`

. . .

40-second render → 4-second render. That is the difference between rendering
constantly and avoiding it.

## Journal-ready YAML

```yaml
bibliography: references.bib
csl: vancouver.csl
format:
  docx:
    reference-doc: journal-template.docx
  pdf:
    linenumbers: true
```

. . .

Rejected by one journal, reformatting for the next = **one line**.

::: {.notes}
🎯 The csl swap is the demo that wins the room. Do it live: Vancouver → APA,
re-render, references reformat.
:::

## Publish

```bash
quarto publish gh-pages
```

One command. Renders, pushes, gives you a URL.

. . .

**Check what you are publishing.** Raw data in `data/`, a path with a patient
ID, an unanonymised `glimpse()`. Public is permanent.

## Group activity — 45 min {background-color="#0f5257"}

Turn yesterday's `report.qmd` into a structured manuscript.

Skeleton is on the website.

::: {.notes}
📋 Rotate the typist every 15 min. Render early — a document that has never
rendered fails at the deadline.
:::
